findings.title: Mixed Symbol/String types in fallback list cause stale-cache misses
findings.body: self[locale] returns [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]. The first element is whatever locale was passed in (often a String, because set_locale assigns I18n.locale from SiteSetting.default_locale or current_user.effective_locale, both Strings), while the remaining two are Symbols. Array#uniq does not deduplicate across these types, so the resulting fallback list mixes Strings and Symbols. When ensure_loaded! iterates that list and stores entries into translate_accelerator's @loaded_locales, a later lookup with the same logical locale but the other type will miss and trigger a redundant load of the same yml file on subsequent requests.

findings.title: FallbackLocaleList inherits Hash but [] returns Array, breaking Hash semantics
findings.body: class FallbackLocaleList < Hash overrides [](locale) to return an Array of fallback locales instead of a Hash entry. While the standard I18n::Backend::Fallbacks class uses the same trick, this design makes Hash methods such as keys, values, each, merge, and empty? operate on the empty underlying Hash rather than the fallbacks, which is misleading and can break any caller that relies on Hash semantics. A plain class (or subclass of Object) with an explicit [] method would more honestly model what this object is.

findings.title: No tests cover the new fallback behavior or the ensure_loaded! preload
findings.body: The PR changes fallback behavior in several non-trivial ways: it introduces a custom FallbackLocaleList with a fixed [user_locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en] order, eagerly preloads all fallback locales for every request via I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! in ApplicationController#set_locale, removes config.i18n.fallbacks = true from three environment files (production.rb, profile.rb, cloud66 production.rb), and removes config/initializers/pluralization.rb (folding it into the new i18n initializer). No specs are added or updated, and the PR description is just 'Test 9' with no detail, so there is no automated verification that the fallback chain resolves as intended, that ensure_loaded! actually populates @loaded_locales, that background-job code paths still get translations, or that existing fallback-related tests still pass.

findings.title: Fallback chain ignores current_user.effective_locale when site default differs
findings.body: The [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en] chain puts the site-wide default before English but does not include the user's locale's natural parent (e.g. pt_BR users fall back to English rather than pt). While the inline TODO acknowledges this is a future enhancement, the current order also means that a user whose effective_locale happens to equal SiteSetting.default_locale still gets :en listed twice (uniq handles it, but the chain collapses to [default, :en] rather than [user, default, :en]), so any locale-specific translator for that user is silently lost. More importantly, for languages like zh_TW or sr_Latin whose site default may be a closely related variant, the user loses the more-specific fallback path entirely.
